- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.5) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.2) — model ignores downward pressure.
- Model overreacts to recent price spikes — forecasts peak too early and then drop too sharply.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds onto high forecasts longer than actual price reversion suggests.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the window, then underestimate later — especially after sentiment shifts.
- Sentiment correlation: when sentiment is rising, model forecasts lag behind actual price movement by 1–2 days.
- Avoid “sudden drop” after spike — model often predicts a sharp fall after a peak, but true drop is slower or less severe.
- Use sentiment as a filter — if sentiment is >0.4, reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment is <0.2, increase forecast downward bias by 3–5% to reflect subdued market sentiment.
